audit_findings.title: Equity-method pipelines may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: Potential duplicate components: $1.243 billion bridge addition and equity-method earnings of $177 million, $162 million and $138 million for 2023-2025
audit_findings.mechanism: OE may capitalize equity-method earnings while the equity bridge separately adds the same pipeline interests; the $1.243 billion bridge amount equals the latest filed carrying amount of the investments
audit_findings.evidence: The earnings of our unconsolidated joint ventures are included in earnings from equity method investees in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity-method earnings enter reported income and that the latest carrying amount is $1.243 billion. The supplied record does not show whether those earnings were removed from OE, so double counting is unresolved rather than proven. If they remain, the error is large relative to the $1.415 billion total positive bridge and annual OE of $276.9-$387.5 million.
audit_findings.action: Trace each OE year to reported net income, remove equity-method earnings and associated tax effects if present, establish current common-equity value for each stake rather than automatically using carrying value, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued Stonewall litigation could reduce both equity value and recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 damages awarded in the April 2, 2026 order; prior gross loss range was $0-$55 million, or up to $46.75 million at DTM's 85% interest; appeal, attorney fees and any prospective rate effect are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse final judgment would reduce the equity bridge, while an adverse prospective rate interpretation would reduce recurring OE
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates the range of loss to be $ 0 to $ 55 million, and could result in a material impact to the rates charged to Antero going forward.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing supersedes the earlier unresolved trial posture: no damages were awarded and management now considers loss remote. Remaining exposure depends on an appeal, discretionary attorney fees or a later rate consequence, none of which is presently established in the numbers.
audit_findings.action: Monitor appeal deadlines, fee orders and any contract-rate implementation; rerun the bridge and OE only if a final adverse amount or prospective rate reduction emerges.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital may be understated for aging regulated infrastructure
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional integrity, repair or compliance spending would increase the maintenance-capital deduction from OE and reduce the terminal-value cash flow
audit_findings.evidence: We may incur significant costs associated with repair, remediation, preventive and mitigation measures associated with our integrity management programs and may be required to comply with new safety regulations and make additional maintenance capital expenditures in the future for similar regulatory compliance initiatives that are not reflected in our forecasted maintenance capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms that portions of the acquired and legacy systems are more than 50 years old and that future initiatives may require spending outside forecast maintenance capital. It does not identify a current omitted project or amount, while management says costs under presently implemented rules are not expected to be material. This is therefore a forward-looking risk, not a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain asset-level integrity plans, inspection findings, modernization classification, expected outage costs and PHMSA/state compliance budgets; compare them with the maintenance-capital deductions used in each OE year and forecast.

audit_findings.title: The apparent 2025 growth step was principally acquisition-driven
audit_findings.magnitude: $212 million of the $244 million 2025 Pipeline revenue increase was acquisition-related; the anchor is only $12.7 million below the $387.5 million latest-OE cap, limiting the base-case anchor effect to approximately $178 million of equity value or $1.73 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The mixed acquisition perimeter distorts the historical OE trend and may affect growth selection; financing costs and the November 2024 share issuance must also match the earnings perimeter
audit_findings.evidence: Operating revenues increased $244 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to activity from the interstate pipelines acquired in the Midwest Pipeline Acquisition of $212 million, new LEAP contracts of $31 million and higher long-term storage revenue at Washington 10 Storage Complex of $9 million, partially offset by lower Bluestone volumes of $7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the MIN(trend, latest) rule caps any upward anchor correction at $387.5 million. That cap would move base value from $64.85 to about $66.58 per share. Even the supplied bull value of $74.04 remains $55.48 below the $129.52 market price, so the stated valuation conclusion is not reasonably changed. The direction is mixed because a pro forma history may raise the anchor while showing less organic growth.
audit_findings.action: Prepare 2023-2024 pro forma OE for Guardian, Midwestern and Viking, match acquisition debt interest and issued shares to that perimeter, and document the resulting organic growth rate; retain the current conclusion unless the recast reveals a separate OE-level omission.

audit_findings.title: Clean Fuels has contingent and variable economic costs outside the stated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $24 million of the $34 million milestone ceiling remains after the $10 million payment; $8 million of that payment remained as a prepaid asset at June 30, 2026; variable sharing payments are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Milestone obligations may reduce the equity bridge, while variable sharing payments reduce Clean Fuels cash retained in recurring OE
audit_findings.evidence: A gas supply agreement at Clean Fuels Gathering requires contingent payments from DT Midstream of up to $ 34 million upon the completion of certain milestones, including cumulative production and income tax credits, and variable payments under a sharing mechanism.
audit_findings.explanation: The fixed remaining milestone ceiling alone equals about $0.23 per diluted share if deducted directly, only about 0.4% of base value. However, the sharing mechanism is unquantified and could recur alongside Clean Fuels revenue and tax-credit benefits, so the record cannot establish total materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the milestone schedule and sharing formula, forecast payments against production and tax-credit assumptions, verify whether the prepaid amount is already consumed through expenses, and rerun Clean Fuels OE and the bridge on a consistently net basis.

audit_findings.title: The short OE history may retain nonrecurring tax remeasurements
audit_findings.magnitude: 2023 benefit of $18 million, 2024 expense of $15 million and 2025 expense of $2 million; if all remain in OE, consistent normalization computes to an approximately $387 million trend anchor versus $374.8 million, increasing base value by about $1.66 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring tax remeasurements distort annual OE and therefore the three-year log-trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: Our 2023 effective tax rate includes $ 18 million of state and local statutory tax expense offset by the impact of state tax rate changes of an $ 18 million benefit driven by changes in tax status and updates to state apportionment which were completed in 2023 as a part of ongoing corporate tax structuring, simplification initiatives, and initial post-separation full-year tax return filings.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE reconciliation already normalized these items is unresolved. If it did not, removing the 2023 benefit and adding back the 2024-2025 expenses raises rather than lowers the fitted anchor, but the resulting base value remains approximately $66.51 per share versus the $129.52 price. The roughly 2.6% base-value effect is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect each annual OE reconciliation, normalize all three remeasurements consistently while retaining recurring taxes, and update the anchor calculation for audit accuracy.
